missing_spec_content.spec_text: (HT only) Students should be able to use vector diagrams to illustrate resolution of forces, equilibrium situations and determine the resultant of two forces, to include both magnitude and direction (scale drawings only).
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson explains scale drawings for finding a resultant and for equilibrium. For resolution it only states the idea, in keyPoints[3].content: "a single force can be resolved into two components acting at right angles to each other." It never shows how to resolve a force into components using a scale vector diagram.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to apply Newton's First Law to explain the motion of objects moving with a uniform velocity and objects where the speed and/or direction changes.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson gives examples of uniform velocity and of slowing down caused by friction. It gives no example of a resultant force changing an object's direction. It does not state the spec point that "the velocity (speed and/or direction) of an object will only change if a resultant force is acting on the object."

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to estimate the speed, accelerations and forces involved in large accelerations for everyday road transport.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson estimates only a force, using a given acceleration: "A car of about 1200 kg accelerating at about 3 m/s² needs a resultant force of about 1200 × 3 ≈ 3600 N." It does not teach students to estimate typical speeds or accelerations for road transport. It also does not deal with large accelerations such as those in braking or collisions.

above_gcse.text: Inertia is the tendency of objects to resist changes in their motion. A more massive object has greater inertia.
above_gcse.why: The spec marks inertia as "(HT only)". The lesson teaches it as core content with no 'Higher only' label, although it does label other HT content such as inertial mass. Foundation students may think they need to learn it.

above_gcse.text: Free body diagrams show all the forces acting on a single object.
above_gcse.why: In the spec, the use of free body diagrams sits under "(HT only) Students should be able to: ... use free body diagrams". The lesson presents this as core content without a 'Higher only' label.

wrong_terms.text: Friction and air resistance are forces that act against motion. They are what slow real objects down.
wrong_terms.spec_term: resistive forces ("when a vehicle travels at a steady speed the resistive forces balance the driving force")

not_checked: All keyPoints have "diagram": null, so no diagrams or images were checked.

Required practical activity 7 refers to "AT skills ... AT 1, 2 and 3" and to "Key opportunities for skills development (page 96)". Those skill details were not supplied, so the practical's coverage of them could not be checked.
